evidence.quote: These rocks were once covered by softer rocks (i.e. limestone & shale) that have been eroded away. In the vicinity of Bilger's Rocks the remaining sandstone bed measures over 50 feet (15 m) thick

evidence.claim: Mountain-building forces fractured the rock into joints.
evidence.quote: Joints are caused by tectonic, or mountain-building forces that move and stress rocks, causing them to fracture.

evidence.claim: Water enters those cracks, and freezing and thawing push the rock farther apart.
evidence.quote: The resulting cracks provide an inlet for water, which slowly dissolves the rocks and allows space for ice crystals to freeze and thaw during the seasonal cycles, further pushing the rocks apart.

evidence.claim: Plants and trees grow through the crevices, exerting pressure that enlarges the gaps.
evidence.quote: Eventually, plants and trees also grow up through crevasses in the rocks and can exert considerable pressure as they grow, forcing even larger gaps to form.
